scheme_name: National Mission on Edible Oil–Oil Palm: Planting Materials
description:
The National Mission on Edible Oil–Oil Palm is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India in 2021. 

The mission was introduced with the objective of reducing the country's dependency on edible oil imports. 

India is one of the largest consumers of edible oils in the world. 

In 2020-2021, India imported approximately 14 million metric tons of edible oils. 

The mission aims to increase domestic production of palm oil to achieve self-sufficiency. 

The target is to increase the area under oil palm cultivation to 6.5 lakh hectares by 2025-2026. 

The government has set a goal to produce 11 lakh metric tons of crude palm oil by 2025-2026. 

The initiative is expected to reduce the import dependency on edible oils by 10 percent by 2025. 

The National Mission on Edible Oil–Oil Palm focuses on promoting oil palm cultivation in the northeastern states and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. 

The government has identified these regions due to their suitable climatic conditions for oil palm cultivation. 

The mission also aims to provide financial assistance to farmers for the cultivation of oil palm. 

Farmers can receive up to ₹29,000 per hectare for planting materials and other inputs. 

The government has allocated ₹1,100 crore for the National Mission on Edible Oil–Oil Palm in the Union Budget for 2021-2022. 

This allocation is part of a larger initiative to enhance domestic oilseed production. 

The mission is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The Indian Council of Agricultural Research is also involved in research and development activities related to oil palm. 

The mission aims to provide quality planting materials to farmers to ensure better yields. 

Farmers are encouraged to adopt modern agricultural practices for oil palm cultivation. 

The government is promoting the establishment of nurseries for the production of quality planting materials. 

These nurseries will be set up in collaboration with state governments and agricultural universities. 

The mission also emphasizes the importance of training and capacity building for farmers. 

Workshops and training programs will be organized to educate farmers about oil palm cultivation. 

The government aims to create awareness about the benefits of oil palm cultivation among farmers. 

The mission is expected to create direct and indirect employment opportunities in rural areas. 

It is estimated that the cultivation of oil palm can generate around 2.5 lakh jobs by 2025-2026. 

The government has also planned to set up processing units for palm oil. 

These processing units will be established in proximity to oil palm cultivation areas. 

The aim is to ensure that farmers receive better prices for their produce. 

The processing units will also help in reducing post-harvest losses. 

The mission includes a provision for the establishment of a dedicated fund for oil palm cultivation. 

This fund will be utilized for providing financial assistance to farmers and for research activities. 

The government is also working on developing a robust supply chain for palm oil. 

This includes logistics and transportation facilities to ensure timely delivery of inputs and produce. 

The mission is aligned with the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative. 

Atmanirbhar Bharat aims to make India self-reliant in various sectors including agriculture. 

The National Mission on Edible Oil–Oil Palm is expected to contribute significantly to this goal. 

The mission will also help in enhancing the income of farmers. 

The average yield of oil palm is estimated to be around 4 to 5 tons per hectare. 

This yield is significantly higher compared to traditional oilseed crops. 

The government is promoting intercropping with oil palm to enhance farmers' income. 

Farmers can grow other crops alongside oil palm to diversify their income sources. 

The mission also focuses on sustainable agricultural practices. 

Sustainability is a key aspect of oil palm cultivation. 

The government is encouraging the use of organic fertilizers and pest management practices. 

The implementation of the mission is expected to be monitored regularly. 

The Ministry of Agriculture will oversee the progress of the mission. 

Regular assessments will be conducted to evaluate the impact of the mission on farmers' livelihoods. 

The government aims to establish a feedback mechanism for farmers. 

This mechanism will help in addressing the challenges faced by farmers in oil palm cultivation. 

The National Mission on Edible Oil–Oil Palm is part of a broader strategy to enhance oilseed production in India. 

The government has also launched other initiatives to support oilseed farmers. 

These include the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana and the National Food Security Mission. 

The mission is expected to play a crucial role in achieving the goal of self-sufficiency in edible oils. 

The government is committed to providing all necessary support to farmers under this mission. 

The success of the mission will depend on the active participation of farmers. 

Farmers are encouraged to take advantage of the financial assistance and training programs offered. 

The government aims to create a conducive environment for oil palm cultivation in India. 

The National Mission on Edible Oil–Oil Palm is a landmark initiative that holds the potential to transform the edible oil sector in India. 

It is expected to enhance food security and improve the livelihoods of millions of farmers across the country. 

The mission is a step towards achieving sustainable agricultural development in India. 

The government is optimistic about the positive outcomes of this initiative in the coming years. 

Overall the National Mission on Edible Oil–Oil Palm is a comprehensive program aimed at boosting domestic production of palm oil. 

It is designed to empower farmers and ensure economic growth in rural areas. 

The mission is a significant move towards reducing import dependency and enhancing self-reliance in edible oils.
